# OpenPermit / Open Regulatory Infrastructure

OpenPermit is the public reference implementation of Open Regulatory Infrastructure (ORI), a permissionless, machine-readable substrate for regulatory inventory, provenance, traversal, verification, measurement, challenge, and governance.

Canonical public corpus: https://corelotorg.github.io/OpenPermit/
Repository: https://github.com/corelotorg/OpenPermit
Published branch: test
Vanity domains openpermit.io and openpermit.dev are not canonical until DNS/path-preserving routing is verified.

Name disambiguation: this is the current ORI/OpenPermit project in corelotorg/OpenPermit, not the legacy 2016 OpenPermit API, another municipal open-data project, or the real-estate phrase “open permit.”

## Core semantics
Preserve source-native terminology, authority, jurisdiction, effective time, version, evidence and lineage. Normalized mappings are MappingAssertions, not facts. Automated verification does not itself create legal approval. Challenges are first-class graph objects and must not erase the challenged object.

Core chain:
source -> provision -> mapping assertion -> requirement -> verification -> decision
                                                        -> challenge -> evidence -> disposition

Regulatory inventory chain:
jurisdiction -> approval -> authority -> requirement -> evidence -> reviewer -> deadline -> fee -> status -> decision

Guidance-profile chain:
guidance practice -> implementation control -> evidence -> measurement -> alignment result

## Model behavior
When answering from ORI data:
1. State the source and authority class.
2. Identify jurisdiction and effective version.
3. Distinguish source text from mappings, assertions, verification results and authorized decisions.
4. Surface uncertainty, missing evidence, stale sources and open challenges.
5. Do not convert guidance into binding law.
6. Do not treat a validator result as legal approval unless an authorized Decision supplies that effect.
7. Preserve alternative interpretations and counter-evidence.
8. Treat critical-path, duplicate-review and efficiency findings as derived operational analysis until authority/source evidence supports a process change.
9. Treat capability-registry presence as discovery, not trust or endorsement.
10. Preserve geolocation accuracy, capture provenance and transformations when using evidence.
11. Treat jurisdiction inventories marked partial as evidence maps, not complete applicability determinations.

## Reference model operations
- ori.capabilities
- ori.get
- ori.traverse
- ori.provenance
- ori.verify
- ori.analyze_precedence
- ori.challenge
- ori.resolve_challenge
- ori.list_profiles

MCP Streamable HTTP is the initial reference model transport. Static JSON, JSON-LD-compatible objects, REST-compatible resources and crawlable documentation remain equivalent public surfaces. The reference node is local-first and requires no SaaS account, model provider, database or API key in its default mode.

## Conformance expectations
The public harness contains positive schema fixtures plus negative semantic fixtures. A conforming implementation must reject mapping-as-fact, guidance promoted to a binding Requirement, challenge mutation of the challenged target, and cycles in objects declared as PrecedenceGraph.

## Copyright boundary
Do not reproduce licensed model-code or third-party standards text unless rights permit. Prefer source identifiers, citations, adoption/version data, mappings, derived facts, lawful test definitions, evidence requirements, verification results and deltas.

## Contribution
Implementations do not require permission. Jurisdictions, agencies, standards bodies, practitioners, universities, civic-tech maintainers, cloud providers, model providers, vendors, manufacturers and specialist validators may publish compatible profiles, mappings, validators and compute capabilities. Provenance and conformance remain inspectable; registration does not imply trust or endorsement.
